title: AI as a tool, not a co-developer
summary: AI codes well, but it's a hyper-focused lens — not a co-developer with the full picture.
body:
AI is honestly a great tool, I use it and I think it's genuinely useful. But the way I see it right now, it's more like a hyper-focused lens than a co-developer. It can code, and it can code well, I'm not taking that away from it.

What it struggles with though is the full picture. It's going to solve the problem you put in front of it, but it's not necessarily thinking about how that solution ripples out to the rest of your app. It might not catch that it's breaking something else, or that the logic it wrote technically passes your test but isn't actually doing what you meant. You get the output you asked for, not always the output you needed.

And yeah, you can get smarter with your prompts, add more context, be more specific and that helps, it genuinely does. But in my experience there's a ceiling to that. The more complex things get, the more it starts losing the thread of what you were trying to do in the first place.

So look, I'm not knocking it. I use it, I like it. But at the end of the day it's a tool, and you've got to treat it like one. The experience and judgment of knowing why you're building something a certain way, that still has to come from you.
